title: 2026-11-25-virtual-nodes-as-elements — 6. Visual Design Verification: 1 row(s)
body:
## 2026-11-25-virtual-nodes-as-elements — 6. Visual Design Verification: 1 row(s)
**Section:** 6. Visual Design Verification
**Change:** ~ contract/driver-click-refusals/covered · promise: was «A driver click on an element under an open select list is refused `covered`.»; now «A driver click on an element under an open select list is refused `covered`; a virtual node reads `covered` only when an element lies over its region's centre.»
**Why:** contract/driver-click-refusals/covered: A click now takes a virtual id and its covered reading is its region's centre alone, a stated limit the row must carry. — on delegate escher overseer, 2026-11-25, inputs#I2 (F12 A), PROVISIONAL
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-25T09-46-09-wrap/

- Focus: Tab / Shift+Tab via `focus_next_node` / `focus_prev_node`, in every document skipping a node that does not show (out of the document, under `display: none`, or not `visibility: visible`); focusability recomputed on `tabindex` / `href` / `disabled`; removing the focused node drops focus to the root element, the tree's focus naming the window, and runs blur side effects; the tree's focus is the focused node only where it is among the built nodes, else `u64::MAX`, the window, so the tree never names a node it did not build; since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness, in every document (ratified by the founder), a pointer click on a `button` (any type) or an `input` of type `submit`, `reset` or `button` focuses it, then submits the form owner when it is a submit button — a disabled form control still stops the walk first, a disabled ancestor `div` not (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), a click on a `select` focuses it, clearing its typeahead and the document's text selection, and on a drop-down single select also opens its list or closes one standing, a single list box opening none and a click on its row choosing that row alone whatever modifier is held, a disabled select or row changing nothing, two clicks on one point opening then closing, each focusing (a disabled select stopped by the walk's gate first, so it neither focuses nor acts; a click on a row of an open list choosing it, a disabled row changing nothing and leaving the list open and a group header choosing nothing; a press outside the list closing it with no event, and a driver `click` on an element under the list refused `covered`, a virtual node reading `covered` only when an element lies over its region's centre; a label's click on a bound single select focusing it and opening nothing; an option of a closed single select, under a group too, is not clicked — a driver `click` on one is refused `covered`; a click on a `multiple` select's row runs `click_select_row`, a disabled select stopping it, otherwise focusing the select and clearing the typeahead and the text selection, a plain click choosing the row alone, Ctrl or Meta flipping it, Shift spanning and a disabled row changing nothing), and a click on any other non-interactive element (a CRUD row, the list) still clears focus; two pointer clicks on one point within 500 ms and 2 px are a double click, read on the document's clock — on a harness-built document the harness's `VirtualClock`, so two driver `click`s on one point with no `advance` between them are a double click, selecting a word in a text input — while each still focuses its target as one click does (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); `:focus-within` matches the focused element and its ancestors by the `FOCUS_WITHIN` element state, while `:focus-visible` never matches; `:open` matches a `details` or `dialog` carrying `open` by the `OPEN` element state, in every document, flipped when a `details`'s first `summary` toggles it through the mutator — `open_state`'s tests, in both layout modes, read the `open` attribute by presence at construction, move it through a mutator write and removal and a summary's click and Enter, and read `:open` matching. Enter and Space (since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness, in every document, ratified by the founder): a pressed Enter on the focused node that is no disabled form control (`ElementData::is_disabled`; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18 — a `disabled` attribute on a `summary` or an `a` gating neither key, as HTML does) dispatches a Click on a `button`, a `summary`, an `input` of type `submit`, `reset` or `button`, or an `a` with `href`; a released Space (`handle_key_up`) dispatches the same Click on a `button`, a `summary`, or an `input` of type `submit`, `reset`, `button`, `checkbox` or `radio` — a link takes no Space, and a text input and a range input take neither key there; the Click (`Node::synthetic_click_event_data`) runs the app's handlers (a Dioxus `onclick`), then `handle_click`, whose checkbox and radio arms dispatch, after `input`, a `change` with the same value, in every document, a checkbox always and a radio only where it was not checked before the click (`checkable_change_event`), while typing in a text input and a range's key and pointerdown fire `input` and no `change` (`text_range_no_change_event`). Range input (since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction, in every document, ratified by the founder): focused and with no `disabled` attribute (read by presence), it steps up on ArrowRight/ArrowUp, down on ArrowLeft/ArrowDown, goes to its minimum on Home and its maximum on End, every other key doing nothing — each change marks the changed set and fires one `input`, a move that changes nothing none; a click focuses it without moving its value, and a main-button pointerdown sets the value from the hit's fraction of the content box, clamped to [0, 1]. Select: a focused drop-down `select` (no `multiple`, display size 1) that is no disabled form control (`ElementData::is_disabled`), its list closed, takes ArrowDown / ArrowUp to the next / previous enabled option and Home / End to the first / last enabled option (with none chosen, ArrowDown reads as Home and ArrowUp as End), and a character pressed with no Ctrl, Alt or Meta as typeahead — the first enabled option whose label starts with the text typed, compared in lower case, the text kept for one select until 1 s of the document's clock passes; Enter, and a Space with no typed text standing, open its list on press, on the chosen option and firing nothing, a released Space doing nothing more, a disabled, inert, hidden or empty select, or a single list box, opening nothing, and every other key does nothing; each change marks the changed set and dispatches one `input` then one `change`, a key that changes nothing firing none; a focused single list box (a single select of display size above 1) that is no disabled form control takes the arrows, Home and End to step and choose and a printable key with no Ctrl, Alt or Meta as typeahead, the reached row scrolled into view, while Enter, a Space with no typed text and every other key do nothing and no list opens; an `optgroup`'s options are the select's own in tree order, a disabled group's rows reading as disabled. With the list open — an engine overlay on every document, remote pages included — the engine paints it over the page and focus stays on the select: its keys move the highlight over enabled rows and choose nothing, a pointer over an enabled row moving it too; Enter and Space choose the highlighted row and close, Tab in either direction chooses and closes before focus moves, one `input` then one `change` firing and none for the option already chosen; Escape closes with the value unchanged and no event, as a second click, a press outside and a page scroll do, a wheel outside closing it and then scrolling; a close clears the typed text, and a select made inert, disabled, hidden or removed while open closes its list. A list shows at most `MAX_ROWS` 20 and scrolls by key and by wheel, its thumb painted, taking no hit and not draggable, its rows one height, and it opens and closes with no motion. A focused `multiple` select that is no disabled form control takes ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End: alone they choose that row alone, with Shift they span from the anchor (with no cursor yet from the last chosen row), and with Ctrl or Meta they move the current row and change nothing; with a valid `size` a key brings the current row into view through `scroll_into_view`; a Space with no typed text standing flips the current row and with text standing joins it, a character with no Ctrl, Alt or Meta chooses its match alone, its disabled rows are never chosen and Ctrl+A is not modelled; the driver's `type` on any select focuses it with no click, so it fires no DOM focus events on a single select either, closes any list and clears the typeahead, a text opening on a space typing nothing, and the driver's `press` takes an optional `ctrl`, false when absent and held as the host's action key (Meta on macOS, Control elsewhere), so a non-adjacent `multiple` set can be built through the driver.

- Disabled-ness is keyed one way since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness (in every document, ratified by the founder): the `DISABLED` state (`:disabled`) reads the attribute's presence, and the pointer-move gate, `ClickTarget::Disabled`, `handle_click`'s walk gate, the Enter and Space activation and focusability read `ElementData::is_disabled` — that presence on a `button`, `input`, `select` or `textarea` alone (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) — so `disabled="false"` and a bare `disabled` on a form control match `:disabled` and are not focusable, a bare `disabled` set after creation takes its focusability away, and a `<div disabled tabindex=0>` takes focus. dioxus-native-dom removes a falsy value of its 28 boolean attributes — upstream's `is_bool_attr` predicate since 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship (`disabled`, `checked`, `hidden`, `inert` among them; a framework-written `inert: false` is removed, while a truthy `inert` (by presence on itself or an ancestor element) takes focusability, hits and the tree away from its subtree (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) and Tab reaches the buttons under `inert: false`; HTML's focus fixup is built, in every document, so a node holding focus when it comes under `inert`, a subtree moved under an inert box included, gives focus up as the mutator flushes, no DOM `blur` or `focusout` firing; and a focused node that no longer shows gives focus up after each layout, no DOM `blur` or `focusout` firing, while a `display: contents` control and one beside a hidden sibling keep focus (ratified, the Tab walk's skip of unshown nodes remedying the Tab trap the post-layout fixup alone made; a control whose own `:focus-within` rule hides its container still takes Tab and loses focus at the next layout, a stated limit)), so a `hidden: false` element stays displayed, in the tree and in the snapshot; an attribute outside the list holding `false` is still written as `"false"`. The snapshot reads `enabled` by presence (on a virtual node the declaration's disabled flag, `enabled` false where declared disabled) — the driver's `disabled` refusal cause is stated on the same presence reading ("the element carries the `disabled` attribute, which the snapshot reads as not enabled") and is detected on it and on nothing else: the driver refuses a `click` or a `type` as `disabled` when the snapshot reads the element not enabled, with nothing dispatched and focus as it was, and acts on the same control once it reads enabled (`stand_act_disabled.rs`), and the driver's schema defines no role or name set of its own — `checked` a native checkbox's or radio's state, else, on a checkable role, the node's `toggled` reading (`True` true, `False` and `Mixed` false; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), and `value` from the element (a `select`'s `value` `BaseDocument::select_value` — the chosen option's value, for a `multiple` select its first chosen option's in tree order, nothing with none chosen — its options, its children and those under an `optgroup`, kept in the tree as `ListBoxOption` nodes, each `selected` from its chosen state, a closed drop-down's options under it with its select's client rect as their `bounds`, which the driver's visual lint leaves out of its overlap reading in every document with an open list's rows and groups, an open list's row reading its painted row's `bounds` (`Entry.in_select_box`, read through `closed_select_of` for a closed select's option and through `select_list_bounds` for an open list's row or group, never the role) — the stand's flight booker at boot no `overlap`, `stand_lint` reading `[0, 0, 0, 0]` — while a list box's rows and groups, `multiple` or of display size above 1, read their own client rects and its rows are linted as usual; a range input's `value` its current value since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction — `ElementData::range_input_value`, the formatted value a key or a pointerdown moved, while its `value` attribute keeps the boot value; a password input's value reads the fixed mask `MASKED_VALUE` where it holds text and `""` where it holds none, a file input's where its `value` attribute is non-empty — and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a password's typed text is in no painted frame either: blitz-paint paints its value as bullets, its caret at the bullet of its caret index, in every document and through every renderer that paints with blitz-paint, windowed included (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12), two values of one length painting byte-identical frames, focused or not, in both layout modes (`password_painted_masked.rs`); a click inside a field holding a value places the caret by the bullets — `click_password_input` lays out one U+2022 per character through `BaseDocument::layout_as_text_input`, finds the bullet under the point and moves the real editor to that character, so no width of the real characters reaches the caret: two values of one length read one index, in both layout modes (`password_caret_click.rs`; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); the windowed paint is not run; a textarea's typed text reads back as its `value`, proven on an in-file fixture where it is named by `aria-label`), and `focused` from the tree, and `clickable` (a `bool` after `focused`, true where the vdom walk's current listeners hold `click` and the element is no disabled form control; `Snapshot::to_text` writes the token `clickable` after `focused` only when true, and `Snapshot::diff` reads it as `Reading::Clickable`) — focus proven after a click, a Tab press and Shift+Tab (`stand_snapshot_state.rs`). The snapshot's text form (`Snapshot::to_text`) reads that model, never the tree or a control: one line per node, its role and name the node's, with no second mapping (`stand_snapshot_text.rs`). The text's parts (`Snapshot::text_parts`, `TextPart`) are one more reader of that model through the text form and of nothing else — consecutive pre-order lines of `to_text`, never a split line, the parts concatenating to the whole text with every node id on exactly one line — and the driver's `snapshot` reads a screen over `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` in parts: on an over-budget fixture, in both layout modes, each part's lines equal their lines in the whole text, a password's line reads `MASKED_VALUE` in every part, and exactly one line reads `focused` after a click (`stand_snapshot_parts.rs`). The snapshot's diff (`Snapshot::diff`) is one more reader of that model: a text change is reported on the element whose accessible name it changes, by its id and never as a text-run entry, a hidden element leaves and returns with its descendants, and a focus move names exactly the controls whose `focused` reading moved (`stand_diff.rs`). Since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface an MCP tool result is one more reader of that model and of nothing else — a `snapshot` result is `to_text`'s output itself for a whole screen, equal byte for byte to `Session::run`'s screen text in both layout modes (`stand_mcp_tools.rs`), and, for a screen read in parts, its JSON line `{"text","part","parts"}` holding that part's text — through `serve_mcp` a walk's text blocks equal the JSON lines `Session::run` writes, in both layout modes (`stand_snapshot_parts.rs`), its crossing to an MCP client ratified by the founder (2026-10-10). Since 2026-10-12-self-description a password input typed through an MCP `type` reads `MASKED_VALUE` in the tool result, role `PasswordInput` and a non-empty name, the typed text in neither result, in both layout modes — a test-only element of the shared password page `fixtures::password_named` (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/fixtures/mod.rs`), no stand task or app gaining one; and two further readers of the same model state closed words only: the node keys' help that `help` serves (each key's reading, the boolean model's two limits among them) and `DiffNode::differs`, a changed node naming the readings that differ from before the step in node-key order — the Flight Booker's Book names eight nodes — seven that only moved, each `differs` = `[bounds]`, and since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness `flight-book` itself, which the click now focuses, `differs` = `[focused, bounds]` (`stand_diff.rs`). Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot the driver's `screenshot` is one more reader of the model's bounds and of nothing else in it — an element shot, addressed by stable id and refused as every id-addressed call is, is the node's bounds rounded outward and cropped to the part that can be seen — and a shot changes nothing: no focus moves, `has_changes` stays false and the next diff is empty, in both layout modes (`stand_act_screenshot.rs`). The canvas read, which reads one canvas element's draw commands (Circle Drawer's circles and diameter labels leaving only as shot pixels, as the canvas verb's draw commands and as the lint's truncated boxes, no label's text among them), and the virtual-node read, which reads one canvas's declared nodes, are no readers of the snapshot model; a canvas's virtual nodes are served by the reserved id form `{owner}///{key}` in the accessibility tree and, from it, the snapshot and its diff, no element's id holding `///`. Since 2026-11-07-ui-graph the read-only UI graph (`DioxusDocument::graph`, a `UiGraph`, behind `accessibility`) is one more reader beside the snapshot: one `GraphNode` per snapshot node in pre-order but a canvas's virtual nodes, which it excepts, so the actions answer and exploration hold none of them, carrying ids, component names, state names, handler event names, closed flag words and booleans only, never a value, with no second role or name mapping — `stand_graph` asserts in both layout modes that every graph node is a snapshot node and that a graph read changes nothing and holds no typed text. Since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here the driver's `actions` verb (`Session::actions`) is one more read-only reader: for every actionable node (`DioxusDocument::actionable_nodes`, each an `ActionableNode` of `id`, `owner` and `keyed`, read through the one crate-private actionable rule `Readings` it shares with `unkeyed_actionable` — focusable, one of 27 interactive roles, or current vdom-walk listeners holding an event other than `mounted`, so a listener a re-render removed is read by neither) it answers each id-taking verb with the cause `check_target` would refuse it with, changing nothing and writing ids, owner ids, verb and cause words and booleans only, never a value; `keyed` on the carriers is standing — the actionable-key check's wire form, true where the id holds no slash, and Cells' unpaged answer (678 nodes, 106,088 bytes) is a stated limit owned by residual `res-7cc5bi4k`.

- `Document::accessibility_tree` (gated `accessibility`) is what the shell builds — on InitialTreeRequested and, in a redraw after style resolve, when the document's changed set taken there was non-empty, a poll pushing no tree (`changed_nodes`, the nodes written since the last `take_changed_nodes` — a scroll that closes a select's list and its highlight moving to another row marking it, node creation, hover, active, any other scroll and layout alone marking none, a focus lost after a layout marking it; a harness settle neither reads nor drains it and a fresh harness document's set is non-empty, so a check reading `has_changes()` as "this step changed something" drains first) (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07, its windowed witness, at the platform adapter, still owed and owned by residual `res-llkgqygv` (re-carried at 0.3.0, target: next), an active assistive technology this version does not reach, on the founder's F1 (2026-10-14), both halves proven headlessly on the stand since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions; before 2026-10-07 the refresh on change never ran); a `DioxusDocument` overrides it to set each element node's `author_id` to its stable element id — none on `TextRun`, document-root or `Window` nodes; a canvas's virtual nodes are served in this tree, and from it the snapshot and its diff, under the reserved form `{owner}///{key}`, which no element's id holds. The workspace pins the Dioxus crates `default-features = false`: the override — and the snapshot model built on it (`DioxusDocument::snapshot`, which takes role, name and focus from this tree, never a second mapping; its text form `Snapshot::to_text`, that text's parts `Snapshot::text_parts` and its diff `Snapshot::diff` read that model and map nothing again, as does the read-only UI graph `DioxusDocument::graph`, a `UiGraph` of one node per snapshot node but a canvas's virtual nodes, which it excepts, so the actions answer and exploration hold none of them, names and closed words only — the canvas read, which reads one canvas element's draw commands, and the virtual-node read, which reads one canvas's declared nodes, being no readers of the snapshot model —, while the `signal_registry` module (`use_graph_state`, `DeclaredWrite`, `SignalRegistry`) and the reached-handler record (`record_reached`, `reached_handlers`) are not gated) — exists only where a crate names `dioxus-native-dom/accessibility` or depends on one that does (blitz-tests and escher-driver name it; seven_guis names none and gets it through escher-driver, so both its binaries compile these modules — with no platform adapter, so the stand binary still gives no assistive technology a tree). An AccessKit `Adapter` is created before the window is first shown — it panics if the window is already visible.

- `disabled` is keyed one way since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness (in every document, ratified by the founder): the `DISABLED` state (`:disabled`) reads PRESENCE, and the pointer-move gate, `ClickTarget::Disabled`, `handle_click`'s walk gate, the Enter and Space activation and focusability read `ElementData::is_disabled` — that presence on a `button`, `input`, `select` or `textarea` alone (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) — so `disabled="false"` and a bare `disabled` on a form control match `:disabled` and are not focusable, a bare `disabled` set after creation takes its focusability away, and a `<div disabled tabindex=0>` takes focus. dioxus-native-dom removes a falsy value of its 28 boolean attributes — upstream's private `is_bool_attr` predicate, a closed set, since 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship (`disabled`, `checked`, `hidden`, `readonly`, `required`, `multiple`, `selected`, `open`, `autofocus`, `inert` among them; a framework-written `inert: false` is removed, while a truthy `inert` (by presence on itself or an ancestor element, `Node::is_inert`) takes focusability, hits and the tree away from its subtree (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) and Tab reaches the buttons under `inert: false`; HTML's focus fixup is built, in every document: `DocumentMutator::flush` calls `BaseDocument::clear_focus` where `focus_node_id` resolves to a node reading `is_inert()`, with no `inert` arm joining the attribute writes, so a subtree moved under an inert box is covered too; no DOM `blur` or `focusout` fires, and `disabled` takes no part in it, and after each layout a focused node that no longer shows, by `hidden`, `style="display:none"` or CSS alone, gives focus up too, with no DOM `blur` or `focusout` — a `display: contents` control and one beside a hidden sibling keeping focus, and a control whose own `:focus-within` rule hides its container still taking Tab and losing focus at the next layout, a stated limit, a select's choice still moving past its dropped anonymous block, with no panic (`BaseDocument::deallocate_anonymous_block` setting `layout_parent` to `None` on each child still in the slab naming the block), the limit owned by residual `res-6k56erh6`, a line in `escher-0.4.0-incubator/deferred-from-0.3.0.md` and a `CARRY:` on the entry «A11y re-read»), so a `hidden: false` element stays displayed and in the tree; an attribute outside that list holding `false` is still written as `"false"`. The snapshot's `enabled` follows the presence reading, and on a canvas's virtual node the declaration's disabled flag, `enabled` false where declared disabled.

- `Document` trait (`inner`, `inner_mut`, `handle_ui_event`, `poll`, `id`, and under `accessibility` a default `accessibility_tree` a wrapper may override), `BaseDocument`, the document's clock (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18: `DocumentConfig.clock: Option<Arc<dyn Clock>>`, `None` by default and the document then holding a fresh `WallClock` — wall time, as before — read for the overlay scrollbar fade, the double-click window, pan and the fling's generation, the smooth-scroll start and the fling and smooth frames, a sub-document's config carrying its parent's clock; the crate root re-exports `Clock` (`Send + Sync`, `now() -> Duration`), `WallClock` and `VirtualClock` (every clone reading one time, `advance(Duration)` adding with saturation), and no `Instant::now()` or `SystemTime::now()` stands outside `clock.rs` — an API addition flagged upstreamable), `DocumentMutator` (`set_attribute`, `clear_attribute`, removal and insertion restyle through `restyle_for_attribute_change` and `restyle_for_child_list_change`, with no blanket `RestyleHint::restyle_subtree()` but for a `size` or `multiple` write on a select, which restyles its descendants since both decide its rows' presentational hints, and the changed-set insert in `remove_and_drop_all_children` stands first; public `BaseDocument::snapshot_node` takes `attr: &LocalName`, its two callers both in `mutator.rs`; an engine change for every document), `EventDriver`/`EventHandler`, query-selector API, CSSOM (`scrollWidth` and `scrollHeight` answer the CSSOM scroll size, reversed origins included, while the Dioxus mounted-data scroll size stays on Taffy's extent; the resolved `width` and `height` of `resolved_style_value` read `node.unrounded_layout()`, so a reader gets sub-pixel values where `final_layout` rounds; an engine change for every document), scroll API (a box's content measured against Taffy's scrollable overflow, so a reversed box — RTL, row-reverse, column-reverse, wrap-reverse — scrolls to negative offsets, `scroll_to` and `scroll_by` clamping between its scroll minimum and maximum, and after layout rounding every scroll container's offset, the viewport and a running scroll animation clamped to their scroll range and a removed subtree's scroll state reset, so a list whose content shrinks after a delete reads offset 0 (an upstream behaviour change taken); `scroll_into_view` scrolls every scrolling box that holds its target, innermost first, skipping a box whose scroll min and max are both zero, then the viewport — a nested box at once with no scroll event, the requested behaviour for the viewport alone — and on a row of an open select list writes the list's `scroll_y` at once and returns, moving no chain and no viewport; record.title: Virtual nodes inside a canvas
record.requirement: An app declares nodes inside a canvas with an author key, role, name and region, and the driver treats them as elements across the snapshot, diff, click, refusals, UI graph, actions, coverage, layout and exploration; Circle Drawer's circles are virtual nodes
record.observed_gap: A snapshot node needs an author id and a DOM element, so an agent sees a canvas as one opaque element; the UI graph reserves no id form for a non-DOM node; the layout verb reserves an app-canvas placing and the widget trait a commented accessibility tree.

verification.acceptance: On the stand, each Circle Drawer circle reads as a node with its key, role, name and region in the accessibility tree and the snapshot; a click on one acts on its circle and its diff names it; a covered, off-screen, disabled or removed one is refused with that cause; the UI graph, actions, handler coverage, layout explanation and exploration each list it; the circles are reached and acted on by keyboard.

record.notes:
2026-11-25 (2026-11-25-virtual-nodes-declared, wrap P7.3, on the operator's wrap directive point 6): not claimed, its first part proven. A canvas widget declares virtual nodes through the defaulted `Widget::virtual_nodes` (blitz-dom, behind `custom-widget`, additive, nothing sent upstream; overseer1's F2 A, delegate, PROVISIONAL), each a key, AccessKit's `Role` (F4 A), a name and a content-box region. `DioxusDocument::virtual_nodes` reads one canvas's declarations in process, in declaration order: a refused declaration reads its index and one closed reason, `EmptyKey` · `KeyHoldsSlash` · `DuplicateKey` (the first of a key kept) · `EmptyName` · `RegionOutside` (F5 A); each taken node reads the reserved id `{owner}///{key}`; a canvas before its first layout reads `NotLaidOut` and a stale or non-canvas node `NoCanvas`, with no panic. Proven by nine unit cases and `virtual_nodes_declared` in both layout modes (a region fitting the border box but not the content box refused), each refusal arm and the frame held red by controls K1–K14, green on linux, windows and macOS in CI#45538903978 at `a8ee63f0d`. Nothing crosses: `snapshot` and `graph` hold no `///` and no declared name (F3 A defers the names' crossing, the founder's fork), and a declaration change marks nothing and signals nothing (F1 B′, F6 A). Still owed to this capability: virtual nodes as elements in the accessibility tree, snapshot and diff, taking `click` and refused like elements («Virtual nodes as elements»), in every read («Virtual nodes in every read»), on Circle Drawer («Circle Drawer's circles as virtual nodes») and by keyboard («Canvas keyboard path»); the cap stays pooled.

2026-11-25 (2026-11-25-virtual-nodes-as-elements, phase P5): not claimed — not provable by this chunk. This chunk proves, on a fixture canvas a test declares and in both layout modes: the canvas's virtual nodes in the accessibility tree (children of its node, their ids, roles, names and declared disabled state) and from it in the snapshot and diff; `click` on one, settled, its diff naming the node it changed; its refusals `disabled`, `off-screen`, `covered`, `not-found` and `stale`; the id and name over MCP and in a kept check that replays (F3 A, the founder's word). The acceptance's stand surface (Circle Drawer's circles), the UI graph, actions, handler coverage, layout explanation and exploration listing a virtual node, and keyboard reach stay with «Circle Drawer's circles as virtual nodes», «Virtual nodes in every read» and «Canvas keyboard path».

2026-11-25 (2026-11-25-virtual-nodes-as-elements, wrap P7.3, on the operator's wrap directive point 5): not claimed, its second part proven. On a fixture canvas a test declares, in both layout modes: each taken virtual node is a child of its canvas's accessibility node, after its own, with its declared role, its name as label, author id `{owner}///{key}` and disabled where declared (`VirtualNodeDeclaration.disabled`, F8 A with F2 A, the founder's word), under an even-versioned tree id equal to no DOM id; a hidden, collapsed or inert canvas holds none. The snapshot and its diff read it from the tree — id, role, name, `enabled` from the declared state, `clickable` false, bounds its region moved by the canvas's content-box origin. `click` alone takes a virtual id, acts at the region's centre, settles and names the changed node in its diff, and is refused `disabled`, `off-screen`, `covered`, `not-found` or `stale` in the one order with nothing run; `type`, `scroll`, `screenshot` with an id, `layout` and `canvas` read it `not-found` (F10 B, delegate). The id and name cross the snapshot text, diff, MCP results and a kept check that replays — F3 A, ratified by the founder's own word and his confirm of the wrap's answer card. The graph, actions, lint and exploration hold none (F9 A, delegate); a declaration change marks and signals nothing (F11 A, the founder's word). Proven by `virtual_nodes_as_elements` (9 cases; 8 off unix), controls V1 and V3–V8 holding, green 17/17 in CI#45580739068 at `c34877ccd`. Still owed to this capability: the UI graph, actions, handler coverage, layout explanation and exploration listing a virtual node («Virtual nodes in every read»); the stand surface — Circle Drawer's circles as nodes, read on the binary («Circle Drawer's circles as virtual nodes»); keyboard reach («Canvas keyboard path»). The cap stays pooled.
